items.title: Hartalega faces Q3 earnings pressure on softer ASPs, higher costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Analysts expect Hartalega Holdings Bhd to report weaker quarter-on-quarter earnings in the third quarter of financial year 2027 (Q3 FY27), weighed down by the normalisation of average selling prices (ASPs) and a lag in passing higher raw material costs on to customers. CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd expects near-term profitability to come under pressure from the normalisation of ASPs and delays in passing on higher raw material costs to customers, following earlier purchases at elevated prices, potentially squeezing margins. Hartalega Holdings Bhd recorded a core net profit of RM28 million in Q2 FY27, bringing its first-half core net profit to RM99 million.

items.title: Melaka polls: PH hopes for 75pc voter turnout, banks on outstation voters
items.summary: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan is targeting a voter turnout of at least 75 per cent in tomorrow's state election, five percentage points higher than the Election Commission's (EC) target. Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the target was achievable, noting that nearly 30 per cent of the state's electorate comprised voters living outside Melaka, including those in the Klang Valley, southern states and overseas. The EC is targeting a 70 per cent voter turnout in the Melaka election.

items.title: Indonesia faces renewed pressure to sustain investor confidence: analyst
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia faces renewed pressure to maintain investor confidence and economic stability after vice-president Gibran Rakabuming Raka's resignation, with his successor's credibility expected to play a crucial role in shaping market sentiment, an economist said. Business and economic analyst Dr Muhammad Ramaditya said Indonesia's financial markets reacted differently to Gibran's resignation; the rupiah weakened amid political uncertainty, while domestic equities rallied as investors welcomed the prospect of a smoother political transition. Ramaditya said the credibility of Gibran's successor is critical to reassure investors in the political transition.

items.title: Miti says it never cleared Megaspeed, Speedmatrix as Malaysia probes possible AI chip re-exports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) said today it had never cleared Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte Ltd or its Malaysian affiliate, Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd. The ministry said it was working with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department to determine whether any chips imported by the companies had subsequently been re-exported to other countries, and whether the transactions complied with Malaysian law. “Any suggestion otherwise is inaccurate,” the ministry said in a statement today.

items.title: TVET cates record up to 99.1pct employment rate in 2025 - Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) graduates recorded employment rates of up to 99.1 per cent in last year, with more graduates earning RM2,001 and above monthly. "Employment rates among TVET graduates ranged between 86.4 and 99.1 per cent across different qualification levels from 2023 to 2025. "In 2025, advanced diploma and advanced certificate graduates recorded the highest employment rate at 99.1 per cent each, followed by first-degree graduates at 96.6 per cent, diploma graduates at 95.9 per cent and certificate graduates at 95.4 per cent," he said in a parliamentary written reply.

items.title: Miti: No clearance granted to Megaspeed, Speedmatrix
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry clarifies that it has never given clearance or approval to Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte Ltd or its Malaysian affiliate, Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, amid growing scrutiny over the movement of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips. The clarification comes after Megaspeed and Speedmatrix were linked to international concerns over whether high-performance Nvidia chips brought into Malaysia may have been reexported to other countries, including China. The ministry said importing AI chips into Malaysia currently does not require a permit or licence.

items.title: Kepong cop's attacker reported to have mental health issues
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The foreigner who attacked a policeman with a parang in Kepong on Wednesday was believed to have been experiencing mental health issues before the incident. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said investigations revealed that an acquaintance of the suspect had lodged a police report claiming that the man was mentally unstable and had been behaving aggressively at his home. He said policemen, accompanied by personnel from the Fire and Rescue Department and the Health Ministry, went to the premises following the report.

items.title: RM29.6b in housing financing approved under SJKP since 2021
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 114,834 housing financing applications worth RM29.6 billion were approved under the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) between 2021 and August 2026. "The achievement reflects SJKP's role in expanding access to housing financing, particularly for young people and first-time homebuyers who face difficulties meeting conventional financing requirements. The Housing and Local Government Ministry would also strengthen cooperation with state governments, housing agencies and private developers to identify potential new affordable housing developments.

items.title: Trump's interactions with ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in the spotlight
items.summary: JULY 2025: The then-Nvidia CEO met Trump at the White House before Huang's visit to China. AUGUST 2025: Huang met Trump at the White House as the Trump administration and Nvidia engaged in talks over allowing advanced AI chip sales to China. SEPTEMBER 2025: Huang joined Trump during a state visit to Britain.

items.title: Digital Infrastructure Bill to be tabled next year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Digital Infrastructure Bill (Data Centre) is expected to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat next year. Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the bill was in its final stages of drafting and aimed to strengthen the security, resilience and governance of data centres as critical national digital infrastructure. Gobind said the country's growing reliance on digital infrastructure, particularly data centres, made a dedicated legal framework necessary to ensure uninterrupted public services and economic activities.

items.title: Data centre boom prompts new safeguards as Malaysia targets 2027 for regulatory bill
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The Digital Ministry is currently in the final stages of drafting the Digital Infrastructure (Data Centre) Bill. The ministry said the bill aims to create a clearer, more comprehensive regulatory framework to strengthen the protection, operational resilience, and governance of data centres, in line with their importance as the nation’s critical digital infrastructure. The reply responded to Syahredzan Johan’s (PH-Bangi) question on the Digital Ministry’s plan and timeline to introduce a legal framework, such as the Digital Infrastructure Bill, to strengthen the security and resilience of digital infrastructure.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM NOV 13, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Friday, tracking overnight losses on Wall Street amid a decline in Nvidia shares following reports of chief executive officer Jensen Huang's resignation. MMAG Holdings, Parlo and GIIB Holdings were among the most actively traded stocks at the opening bell. Meanwhile, in the cryptocurrency market, Bitcoin traded lower at RM289,278, while Ethereum also declined to RM8,195.

items.title: PublicInvest sets 22 sen fair value on Yes Group, sees 17pct profit growth
items.summary: Analyst Lee Siao Ping said the company's expansion plans, including the establishment of Yes Academy and the growth of its MM2H business, were expected to support a three-year net profit compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of about 17 per cent. "We forecast Yes Group's net profit to reach RM12 million by financial year 2029 (FY29), supported by its European expansion, talent development initiatives and growth in the MM2H segment," he said in a note. Lee said the discount reflected Yes Group's relatively smaller market capitalisation and business scale.

items.title: Selangor sees increase in flood victims, Perak records drop
items.summary: In SELANGOR, the number of victims still being accommodated in seven relief centres has increased to 1,248 victims from 338 families compared to 1,144 victims from 318 families yesterday evening. In addition, Dewan Komuniti Penyayang Tanjung Siam accommodated 50 victims, while Dewan Orang Ramai Hulu Bernam, in Hulu Selangor, accommodated 13 victims. Meanwhile, in PERAK, the number of flood victims in the Hilir Perak district decreased to 288 people from 83 families, compared with 301 people from 87 families yesterday evening.

items.title: Anwar explains move to bring Najib's case before Pardons Board in 2023
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he brought Datuk Seri Najib Razak's pardon application before the Pardons Board in 2023 to ensure that his right to seek a pardon was not denied. He said every prisoner had the right to submit an appeal to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong for consideration under the Federal Constitution. he said.

items.title: Sibu fatal stabbing: Police round up 14 more suspects as arrests climb to 23
items.summary: Sibu district police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said police arrested all 14 suspects at several locations around Sibu yesterday following intelligence operations. They were remanded until Nov 15. Abang Zainal Abidin said police were investigating the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code and working to establish each suspect’s role and involvement.

items.title: Melaka polls: EC targets 70 per cent voter turnout
items.summary: JASIN: The Election Commission is targeting a 70 per cent voter turnout in the Melaka election tomorrow. He also advised voters to cast their ballots early to avoid any inconvenience, particularly with rain forecast in some areas tomorrow. On other matters, Azmi said the EC would continue using the Optical Character Recognition-Voter Attendance (OCR-VA) system to collect and display voter attendance data in real time.

items.title: RHB keeps "Buy" on Johor Plantations, cuts target price to RM2.00
items.summary: In a note, RHB Research said JPG's third-quarter financial year 2026 core profit doubled quarter-on-quarter (QoQ), supported by higher fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production and lower unit costs. Core profit rose 100.4 per cent QoQ to RM176.9 million, although it declined 13 per cent year-on-year (YoY), representing 70 per cent and 63 per cent of RHB Research's full-year and consensus estimates, respectively. The research house said FFB output increased 35.6 per cent QoQ, while the 12.6 per cent YoY decline reflected the seasonal crop cycle.

items.title: New Zealand home prices fall in October, sales cool on cost pressures
items.summary: SYDNEY: New Zealand home prices slipped in October as higher living costs and a weak job market weighed on buyer sentiment, the Real Estate Institute of New Zealand (REINZ) said on Friday. Seasonally adjusted median house prices fell 0.7 per cent from September and were down 3.4 per cent from a year earlier, REINZ data showed. "October's data shows a market that remains measured," said REINZ chief executive Lizzy Ryley.

items.title: Holiday rental boom squeezes out residents in Spain's Malaga
items.summary: MALAGA: Carlos Carrera Lopez has long lived in central Malaga but fears his neighbourhood in the southern Spanish city is slowly disappearing as holiday rentals and mass tourism drive residents out. "We are fighting to ensure this neighbourhood remains inhabited," the 53-year-old doctor, who heads the Old Town residents' association, told AFP, warning of a "mass exodus" caused by mounting tourist pressure. said Francisco Lopez, 52.

items.title: US existing home sales fall to lowest level since 2010
items.summary: NEW YORK: Sales of previously owned US homes dropped to a more than 16-year low in October due to the drag from higher lending rates, a US realtors association said Thursday. "Home buying is difficult when mortgage rates have climbed to their highest levels since 2000, aside from a single month in 2023, said NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun. "As a result, home sales fell to their lowest level since August 2010."

items.title: Kedah MB Sanusi’s 20-year-old daughter injured after motorcycle skids into drain near Alor Setar
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Nov 13 — The daughter of Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor was injured in an accident near Kampung Alor Setol here yesterday. Kota Setar police chief ACP Syed Basri Syed Ali said the 20-year-old, a student at Kolej Islam Darul Ulum in Pokok Sena, sustained injuries to her face and left hand, and was suspected of having fractured her right wrist. “Preliminary investigations found that the accident occurred at about 4pm when the victim was riding a Yamaha X-Max 250 motorcycle from her college in Pokok Sena towards Alor Setar.

items.title: Anwar says he backed Najib’s pardon application to protect every prisoner’s constitutional right to appeal
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that his decision to bring former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak’s pardon application to the Pardons Board in 2023 was to ensure every prisoner’s constitutional right to submit an appeal was not denied. Every prisoner has the right to submit an appeal to the King for consideration. What right?

items.title: SpaceX, Tesla merger talks progress
items.summary: The proposed merger would unify Elon Musk's AI, robotics, EV and aerospace ambitions under a single corporate roof, though it faces steep regulatory hurdles over SpaceX's US defence contracts and Tesla's reliance on China. SpaceX and Tesla could not be immediately reached for comment on the report. SpaceX and Tesla also have a chip manufacturing joint venture, Terafab.

items.title: Inflation, legal system abuse cost liability insurers up to US$337bil in past decade
items.summary: Triple-I said that the additional losses were between 16 per cent and 19.6 per cent of total booked losses. Inflation has added up to US$120.1 billion in losses and cost containment expenses, or 10.8 per cent of booked losses. In commercial auto, additional costs accounted for up to US$86 billion, or up to 34 per cent of booked losses.

items.title: Bollywood bolsters security as underworld fears return
items.summary: MUMBAI: It sounds like a Bollywood thriller, but a spate of shootings and extortion threats targeting Mumbai's stars has sent the industry scrambling for bodyguards, reviving memories of the underworld's grip on cinema in the 1990s. Police have linked the latest violence to the gang of Lawrence Bishnoi, a convicted Indian gangster accused by US prosecutors of directing a global criminal network from behind bars. "Stars are moving around with bodyguards on either side," actor and security agency owner Ronit Roy said.

items.title: Mercedes to halt German investments, mulling plant closures
items.summary: FRANKFURT: Struggling German carmaker Mercedes-Benz announced Thursday it will halt all investment in Germany and is mulling plant closures, underlining the woes facing the country's automotive sector. Like its German peers, Mercedes has been battered by Chinese competition and high costs and last month became the third big German carmaker to cut its outlook for the year. "The executive board has jointly decided to halt all further investments in German sites," said board member Michael Schiebe in an interview posted on the company's intranet and sent to AFP.

items.title: US starts 2027 fiscal year with record October budget deficit of US$404bil
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US government started the 2027 fiscal year with a US$404 billion budget deficit for October, a record for the month and an increase of US$120 billion or 42 per cent from the year-earlier period, as receipts shrank and outlays grew sharply, the Treasury Department said on Thursday. October 2026 receipts fell by US$35 billion, or 9.0 per cent, to US$369 billion, due partly to a 39 per cent drop in net customs collections to US$19.2 billion from US$31.3 billion in October 2025, when President Donald Trump's global tariff revenues reached their peak. Gross interest on the federal debt also rose US$11 billion, or 11 per cent, from the previous October to US$115 billion.

items.title: Nearly 8,000 rescuers, 226 boats ready as Kelantan braces for North-east Monsoon floods
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) had also allocated RM300,000 in operational funds to the Kelantan State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) to prepare for the monsoon season. He said Nadma had also provided two complete sets of Incident Command Post (PKTK) tents, in addition to allocating RM330,000 to the state committee to procure 22 rescue boats with engines and life jackets to strengthen operational capacity in high-risk areas. He said personnel deployment, volunteer training and early evacuation mechanisms were also coordinated through the state and district disaster management committees, together with relevant response agencies.

items.title: Malaysia's BrahMos missile acquisition remains at exploratory stage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's proposed acquisition of India's BrahMos supersonic cruise missile remains at the exploratory stage, with no decision made on the procurement. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the proposal was first raised during preliminary government-level discussions in conjunction with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's official visit to India in September. "The assessment would cover operational requirements, compatibility with existing platforms, systems integration, upgrade requirements and life-cycle costs," he said in a written parliamentary reply to Datuk Seri Ikmal Hisham Abdul Aziz (PN-Tanah Merah).

items.title: Malaysia willing to investigate Speedmatrix over Nvidia chip controversy if authorities make formal request
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Malaysia is ready to facilitate any formal request to investigate Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. However, he said, the government is yet to receive any such request. Johari said this when asked on whether the government has received a formal request to probe Speedmatrix, a Malaysian unit of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International.

items.title: Eppendorf invests RM190mil in Penang for first Southeast Asian manufacturing hub
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: German life sciences company Eppendorf SE is investing about RM190 million to establish its first manufacturing facility in Southeast Asia at Bandar Cassia Technology Park, Penang. The investment marks a significant expansion of the company's global production network, with the facility expected to begin production gradually in 2028 and employ about 130 people by end-2029. Chow said the investment would strengthen Penang's manufacturing landscape while supporting the state's efforts to diversify into higher-value industries, particularly scientific and measuring equipment.

items.title: PM Anwar lands 13th spot in world’s 500 most influential Muslims list for 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has been ranked 13th in the 2027 edition of The Muslim 500: The World’s 500 Most Influential Muslims , published by the Jordan-based Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre (RISSC). According to the 18th annual edition accessible at https://themuslim500.com, the publication noted that Anwar assumed office as Malaysia’s 10th Prime Minister in November 2022, leading the Unity Government under the Pakatan Harapan coalition. Anwar reiterated that Malaysia’s absolute non-recognition of Israel is permanent,” it said.

items.title: #NSTviral: Raw chicken carried in open baskets raises hygiene concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A video showing baskets of raw chicken being transported uncovered in the back of a four-wheel-drive along a highway has sparked concerns over food hygiene and halal compliance. Threads user acsoneg02, who uploaded the video, told the New Straits Times that it was recorded along the New Pantai Expressway (NPE) near Pantai Dalam today. "After the halal chicken incident, I stopped eating chicken and am now willing to eat eggs every day.

items.title: For a stronger safety culture, safety must become a way of life
items.summary: Despite numerous awareness campaigns, safety programmes and enforcement measures, many people continue to take unnecessary risks, ignore safety precautions and underestimate the dangers associated with their everyday activities. Whether involving road safety, water activities or outdoor recreational activities, authorities must ensure that safety requirements are complied with. Every individual must recognise that safety begins with oneself.

items.title: Hajiji says Sabah welcomes tech investors, but warns big projects must protect water and power supplies
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 13 — The Sabah government is open to credible investments in the technology sector, including the development of artificial intelligence (AI) data centres, but every investment proposal must undergo rigorous evaluation to ensure that the interests of the people and the state’s basic infrastructure requirements are not compromised. Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said the state government’s openness to investments and strategic partnerships must be accompanied by due diligence and responsible decision-making, particularly for large-scale projects requiring substantial energy and water resources. The statement was issued in conjunction with the signing ceremony of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) for the proposed establishment of Sabah’s first Artificial Intelligence Data Centre (AIDC) here yesterday, with Hajiji’s speech delivered by Deputy Chief Minister II and Sabah Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun.

items.title: Hilir Perak CDF rescuers stay on high alert amid monsoon flood risks
items.summary: TELUK INTAN: More than 19 years of experience in handling flood disasters have not made rescue operations any easier, with each Northeast Monsoon season in Hilir Perak district demanding greater vigilance, preparedness and commitment. Hilir Perak District Civil Defence Officer Captain Mohd Affindi Ishak said the challenging nature of the operations required personnel to remain on duty around the clock, working in shifts to ensure flood victims were safely evacuated to nearby temporary relief centres. Apart from rescue operations, Mohd Affindi said CDF personnel also closely monitored water levels in high-risk areas to detect any changes and respond quickly when needed.

items.title: Zahid says second phase of refugee registration programme could roll out soon for UNHCR cardholders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The government is expected to launch the second phase of the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme soon, targeting United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cardholders not held at Immigration Detention Depots (DTIs). Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the programme to register Myanmar refugee communities nationwide remained in its first phase, targeting individuals at Immigration Detention Depots (DTIs). Ahmad Zahid said the National Security Council (MKN), Prime Minister’s Department, was working closely with relevant ministries and agencies to hold engagement sessions to obtain feedback and formulate appropriate measures to address issues concerning refugees in Malaysia.

items.title: Hadi hopes BN-PN cooperation continues beyond Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA: The cooperation between Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional is being strengthened as part of efforts to rebuild unity among Muslims in Malaysia, Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said. "The cooperation between BN and PN in Melaka is stronger than what we saw in Negri Sembilan and Johor. Also present were Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan, MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong, PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin and Parti Pejuang Tanah Air (Pejuang) president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir.

items.title: Nacsa on amber alert, but Fahmi says no worrying cyber incidents confirmed so far
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 13 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that based on daily reports received from the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa), no particularly worrying cybersecurity incidents had been confirmed so far. He said Nacsa’s readiness level was currently at amber alert, or moderate, following claims of cyberattacks circulating on social media recently. “I receive daily reports from Nacsa and so far, the agency has not reported any particularly worrying incidents.

items.title: #NSTviral: 'Don't eat it' — Online users rally to save parrotfish
items.summary: The discussion began after Threads user firdausi_68 posted photos of several parrotfish displayed on ice alongside other seafood, as well as one of the fish cooked and served on a plate. "Is this green fish sold in Malaysia? "Why are these fish traders still selling this fish?

items.title: Anwar wants another sit-down with Loke before deciding on Transport Minister’s resignation
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants to hold further discussions with Anthony Loke over the Seremban MP’s resignation as Transport Minister. Anwar said he had yet to make a decision on Loke’s resignation letter, which he had received earlier, as he wanted to discuss the matter with him first. “Yes, Loke did write to me tendering his immediate resignation, but as Prime Minister, I have not accepted it.

items.title: PM Anwar hits back at claims he defied King over Najib’s house arrest controversy
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has denied allegations that he or the government had acted against the wishes of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia over the issue of implementing house arrest for former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak. The Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman said his administration had always upheld the constitutional monarchy system and adhered to established legal processes. Anwar said the decision to place him under house arrest did not fall within his authority as Prime Minister, while the Attorney-General’s decision to bring the matter to court aligned with his responsibility to uphold the rule of law.

items.title: MediAsas: What Malaysians need to know about the new basic medical insurance plan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Malaysians struggling with rising medical insurance premiums may have a more affordable option when MediAsas, a basic medical insurance and takaful plan, is rolled out nationwide in late January 2027. Can existing medical insurance policyholders switch to MediAsas? What makes MediAsas different from conventional medical insurance?

items.title: Can an ageing Malaysia take inspiration from super-aged Japan’s LTC insurance?
items.summary: Before that, can we put in place a long-term care insurance? In 2000, Japan introduced its national long-term care insurance via a mandatory social insurance system, and was described by the International Labour Organization (ILO) as the first in Asia to do so. This co-payment will kick in only when you use the insurance for care services.

items.title: PKFZ ready to open records, facilitate audits amid cooking oil traceability concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ) says it is prepared to provide relevant reports and facilitate regulatory audits amid concerns over the origin, authenticity and traceability of cooking oil products allegedly blended before being re-exported under Malaysian labels. These include the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB), SIRIM, the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS) and the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB). His remarks came after The Edge reported on Nov 4, citing industry sources, that imported palm oil was allegedly being blended with local supplies before being re-exported, potentially allowing foreign-origin oil to be marketed as Malaysian palm oil.

items.title: Najib’s house arrest: Malaysian Bar entitled to challenge Pardons Board decision, says Azalina
items.summary: BANGI, Nov 12 — The Malaysian Bar has the right to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Bar is entitled to mount such a challenge if it believes it has grounds to question the decision. The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) today objected to the Malaysian Bar’s bid to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest.

items.title: KTMB: MyKomuter50 pass activation begins Nov 16, offering 30 days of unlimited travel on selected routes from Dec 1
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The public can start activating the MyKomuter50 Pass on November 16 to enjoy unlimited travel for 30 days on selected KTM Komuter services for RM50, with savings of up to 88 per cent, effective December 1. Alternatively, users can obtain immediate verification at ticket kiosks or counters at KTM Komuter stations. KTMB said activation and purchase facilities would be available at 34 selected stations, comprising 10 KTM Komuter Northern Sector stations, 20 Klang Valley KTM Komuter stations and four Southern Shuttle stations.

items.title: Anwar joins Pakatan campaign trail in Melaka ahead of Saturday’s state polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 12 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim joined the coalition’s campaign trail in Melaka today as campaigning intensified ahead of Saturday’s state election. Anwar’s evening itinerary included the Melaka Rumah Kita programme at the Hang Tuah Jaya parliamentary service centre in Bukit Baru, followed by Melaka Rumah Kita carnival at Taman Melaka Perdana in Alor Gajah. In the 16th Melaka polls, PH is fielding the most candidates, contesting 24 of the 28 state seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (23), Parti Bersama Malaysia (16), Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (seven), Perikatan Nasional (five) and Parti Bumiputera Perkasa Malaysia (one).

items.title: Malaysia’s FRIM puts century-old library collection online, opening 77,600 digital files to public
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — More than a century’s worth of knowledge and information on tropical forest biodiversity and science from the Forest Research Institute Malaysia (FRIM) is now accessible worldwide through its digital repository, the FRIM Research Depository (FRED). FRIM said in a statement today that the FRED portal, fully operational since last year, recorded an average of 2,885 user accesses annually and offered free registration for round-the-clock access to 160,244 metadata records and 77,600 digital files. Besides preserving heritage manuscripts from physical deterioration, the library houses four major special collections, namely the Rattan Collection, Bamboo Collection, Asean Collection and FRIRO (FRIM Research Output) Collection.

items.title: Malaysia selects Turkiye as preferred alternative missile supplier for Navy’s LCS project, says defence minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Turkiye has been selected as the preferred country to supply an alternative to Norway’s Naval Strike Missile (NSM) for the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the decision was made after the government evaluated proposals from several countries, including Turkiye, France and Italy, based on price, delivery timelines and upfront costs. Mohamed Khaled said the missile from Turkiye was of the same type as that already ordered for the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project, allowing supplies to be obtained earlier, as early as 2028.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia must tap China ties to grow exports and open markets for local products
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Malaysia should make the most of its strong ties with China to boost exports and expand markets for local products, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the Madani Government would continue to strengthen the business environment and help micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) expand their reach in international markets. Anwar said the government fully supported this year's conference as a strategic platform to strengthen trade, investment and business networks between the corporate communities of both countries.

items.title: Twelve Filipinos, including six children, detained in Labuan immigration crackdown
items.summary: LABUAN, Nov 12 — Twelve Filipino nationals, including six children, were detained for suspected immigration offences during an enforcement operation on this duty-free island early today. Labuan Immigration Department director Mohd Redzuan Nawi said the operation, codenamed Op Sapu, was conducted from 11pm yesterday to 1.30am today, involving 15 officers who inspected 84 individuals at several locations, including a residential settlement. Mohd Redzuan said the department would continue enforcing the Immigration Act 1959/63, Passports Act 1966, Immigration Regulations 1963 and Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (Atipsom).

items.title: Consumers in Malaysia may soon be able to check chicken’s halal status under proposed new rules
items.summary: Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the move was among efforts to strengthen protection for Muslim consumers following concerns raised by members of parliament over the monitoring and transparency of the halal status of chicken supplies. He said KPDN also agreed with a proposal by Datuk Idris Ahmad (PN-Bagan Serai) that responsibility for ensuring the integrity of the halal supply chain should not rest solely with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) and state religious authorities, but should also involve KPDN in enforcement and local authorities (PBT) in monitoring business premises. “Therefore, KPDN will propose better coordination with state religious authorities, local authorities and the Health Ministry to improve the monitoring of slaughterhouses and chicken sales premises,” he said in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Four foreigners arrested over robbery, assault of cop in Penang; remanded for six days until Nov 17
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 12 — Penang police have arrested four Pakistani nationals, including two women, to assist in investigations into a robbery in which a 43-year-old policeman was injured by suspects armed with sharp objects near a petrol station in Permatang Pauh on Tuesday. Penang Chief Police Officer Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the four suspects, aged between 23 and 36, had been remanded for six days until November 17 to facilitate investigations. The policeman was injured after being robbed by four suspects armed with sharp objects near the entrance to a petrol station in Jalan Samagagah, Permatang Pauh, on Tuesday.

items.title: Man hanging cat from four-wheel-drive vehicle in Kluang sparks online outrage
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 12 — A video and an image showing a man hanging a cat by its neck from the window of a four-wheel-drive vehicle in Kluang, Johor, have sparked outrage on social media. Several social media posts claimed the incident took place at Batu Dua, Jalan Mersing, in Kluang. Kluang police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said police had not received any reports regarding the alleged incident.

items.title: Malaysia approves 143 posts for new Public Defender’s Office, says Azalina
items.summary: “This marks a new chapter for the Legal Aid Department (JBG). As we discussed during the debate on amendments to the Legal Aid and Public Defence Act 2025, we looked at the roles the government should play alongside the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK), as a substantial amount of government funding goes directly to YBGK. She said the initiative would complement the existing legal aid services provided by JBG under the Legal Aid Act by offering another avenue for alternative dispute resolution.

items.title: Malaysia’s fiscal reforms set to lower federal debt ratio to 63.7pc by 2027, says Treasury sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Madani government is committed to gradually reducing the fiscal deficit from 5.5 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2022 to 3.3 per cent in 2027. Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said the reduction in the fiscal deficit reflects the government’s commitment to strengthen the country’s financial position, thereby helping to lower the ratio of the federal government’s debt to GDP. He said the government still prioritises efforts to increase people’s income, including through a minimum wage increase.

items.title: Anwar chairs special meeting as Selangor steps up efforts to tackle recurring floods
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today chaired a special meeting on Selangor flood disaster coordination at Parliament House to streamline efforts to address recurring floods in the state. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the meeting focused on four key actions, including strengthening early warning systems with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) and improving disaster management coordination by the Selangor State Disaster Management Committee. Amirudin said the meeting was also attended by state government representatives, state executive councillors, state assemblymen, district officers, and relevant agencies, including the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), DID, the Public Works Department (JKR), and the Selangor Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU).

items.title: Kelantan reassigns Culture and Heritage portfolio to Zamakshari Muhamad after Kamaruddin Mohd Noor dropped from exco
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 12 — Kelantan Youth, Sports, NGOs and Community Unity Committee chairman Zamakshari Muhamad has been entrusted with overseeing the state’s Culture and Heritage portfolio. He said Kelantan had a distinct cultural identity, rich in historical values, traditions, arts and local wisdom, which formed part of the identity of its people. “I will focus on efforts to preserve and document historical heritage and customs, as well as strengthen local arts and culture in line with Islamic principles and the values of Kelantan society.
